notes:
ACCESS: us.hay.com is retired - it 301s to https://www.dwr.com/brands-hay (Design Within Reach, HAY's US retailer), whose HAY brand page is a brand/designer filter listing and is barred by the brief, so rows come from www.hay.com, HAY's own US-facing English catalogue - the same source the prior Home-Decor pass for this SR used. Reached by plain direct fetch (probe.fetch, no proxy). robots.txt is 'User-agent: *' with no Claude/anthropic-ai directive. Re-fetching 4 furniture PLPs with Cookie 'Hay.countrySelected=USA' returned identical tile counts (13/52/0/12), confirming one global catalogue.

TREE: taken from the site's own mega-menu (there is no /products/furniture landing page - it 404s). Furniture department = Seating (Bar Stools, Benches, Chairs, Lounge, Seat Cushions, Sofas, Stools), Tables (Coffee & Side, Conference & High, Desks, Dining & Cafe, Frames & Spare parts), Beds, Shelves, Wardrobe, Outdoor (Seating, Tables + 9 named collection pages), New Furniture, New Order System. I crawled every furniture URL recursively to find sub-pages the menu does not show.

QTY METHOD: www.hay.com publishes NO product-count header anywhere - no 'N items', no 'N products', no pagination total, no Algolia/Next/structured count (grepped; the only 'results' strings belong to the site-search typeahead widget). So every qty is method 3, full enumeration. Each PLP grid is a MixItUp list with pagingSettings pagingEnabled:false and showCount:0, so the complete list is server-rendered in the first response and 'show more' merely unhides existing .mix-item nodes. I counted distinct /hay/... product-detail URLs, not hrefs: tiles come in two flavours (.hayproduct and, for a few products, imagewithlinkblock) and I accounted for every mix-item on every page as product / sub-page link / intro-text block, so nothing is silently dropped or double-counted. 14 categories were read twice (second read cache-busted) and every number was identical - no session drift.

COLLECTION HANDLING: HAY nests product families under some categories. For Chairs, Sofas and Shelves the family/system sub-pages hold products that appear NOWHERE on the parent PLP (verified by set intersection: zero overlap), so the category's real listing is split across those pages and I report the exhaustive de-duplicated union, flagged, with the hub-only figure stated in each flag. The family pages themselves are NOT emitted as rows (brief section 3 bars 'Collections'). For Outdoor the 9 named collection pages (Palissade, Crate, Hee, Deville, Traverse, Weekday, Balcony, Palissade Cantilever, Palissade Cord) are cross-cuts that are almost entirely redundant with Outdoor Seating + Outdoor Tables - their only non-redundant products are 10 outdoor seat cushions and 1 furniture cover, all out of scope - so Outdoor Seating and Outdoor Tables are the correct leaves and the collection pages are dropped.

EXCLUDED, with reason: Seating > Seat Cushions (17 items, all seat pads/cushions = textiles); Tables > Frames & Spare parts (5 items, all /hay/furniture/tables/table-accessory = furniture parts); Furniture > New Furniture and New Order System (new-arrivals / info landing pages, brief section 3); the 14 outdoor and chair and sofa family collection pages (brief section 3). Accessories department checked node by node for stray furniture and none found: indoor-living/office = 6 desk accessories (pen, notebook, bins, laptop cover, tool box); indoor-living/storage = 3 Colour Storage boxes; indoor-living/wardrobe = 5 hooks/hangers/coat-rack accessories; accessories/bedroom = 16 duvet covers, pillowcases, bedspreads and pyjamas; accessories/bathroom = 24 towels, mats, shower curtains, bathrobes (no vanity units); accessories/flooring = 18 rugs and mats; colour-crate = 5 crates/lids; dogs = 10 pet items; travel = 18 bags/umbrellas; outdoor-living/terrazza-collection = 9 parasols/cushions/tablecloth; outdoor-living/outdoor-market-by-jasper-morrison = 29 picnic/BBQ accessories of which only 4 are furniture (folding chair, sofa, stool, table) - the node's primary product type is outdoor accessories, so it is out.

SANITY CHECKS: numbers differ per category (no site-wide constant); no suspiciously round figures; every page's h3/title matched the category requested and the final URL never redirected; sitemap-products.xml was deliberately NOT used for counts because the prior pass proved it is a superset that retains discontinued products (51 table-lamp URLs vs 31 live tiles).
